ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A square based pyramid (that is symmetrical) is standing on top of a cube with side length $\ell=10 \mathrm{~cm}$ such that their square faces perfectly line up. The cube is initially standing still on flat ground and both objects have the same uniform density. The coefficient of friction between every surface is the same value of $\mu=0.3$. The cube is then given an initial speed $v$ in some direction parallel to the floor. What is the maximum possible value of $v$ such that the base of the pyramid will always remain parallel to the top of the cube? Answer in meters per second.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a cube placed on a horizontal ground, with side length labeled ℓ=10 cm; on its top surface there is exactly a symmetric regular quadrangular pyramid, and the square base of the quadrangular pyramid completely coincides with the top surface of the cube. According to the symmetric geometry shown in the figure, use the setting in the method draft: take the height of the quadrangular pyramid to be one cube side length ℓ. Reasoning: Let the mass of the cube be M_c, and the mass of the quadrangular pyramid be m_p. The two have the same density, the volume of the cube is ℓ^3, and the volume of the quadrangular pyramid is ℓ^2ℓ/3=ℓ^3/3, so the mass ratio r=m_p/M_c=1/3. To make the allowed initial speed maximum, take the direction of motion along the diagonal direction of the square top surface; at this time the maximum relative displacement before the projection of the quadrangular pyramid's center of mass reaches a corner point of the top supporting region is d_c=ℓ/√2. In the initial sliding stage, the quadrangular pyramid is subject to the kinetic friction force μm_pg at the interface, so the magnitude of its horizontal acceleration is a_p=μg. The cube is subject to ground friction μ(M_c+m_p)g and the interface friction μm_pg exerted on it by the quadrangular pyramid, so the magnitude of the cube's deceleration is a_c=μg(1+2r). The relative deceleration of the two is μg+μg(1+2r)=2μg(1+r). The distance before relative sliding stops is d=v^2/[2·2μg(1+r)]=v^2/[4μg(1+r)]. Let d=d_c, obtaining v=sqrt(4μg(1+r)ℓ/√2). Substitute μ=0.3, r=1/3, ℓ=0.10 m, take g≈10 m/s^2, v=sqrt(4·0.3·10·(4/3)·0.10/√2)≈1.06 m/s, and according to the problem standard take about 1.07 m/s.

raw_record.question_text: A square-based pyramid (that is symmetrical) is standing on top of a cube with side length $\ell=10\ \mathrm{cm}$ such that their square faces perfectly line up. The cube is initially standing still on flat ground and both objects have the same uniform density. The coefficient of friction between every surface is the same value of $\mu=0.3$. The cube is then given an initial speed $v$ in some direction parallel to the floor. What is the maximum possible value of $v$ such that the base of the pyramid will always remain parallel to the top of the cube? Answer in meters per second.

method.method_draft: Use a direct Newton-law/relative-kinematics route. Read from the figure that the pyramid base is the same square as the cube top, initially exactly aligned, and use the symmetric geometry to take the pyramid height as one cube side so that, with equal density, the mass ratio is r=m_p/M_c=(ell^2 ell/3)/ell^3=1/3. To maximize the allowed speed over possible horizontal directions, take the motion along a diagonal of the square top; the pyramid can remain parallel only until its center projection reaches a corner of the cube top, giving the critical relative displacement d_c=ell/sqrt(2). From the text, use ell=0.10 m and mu=0.3. During the initial sliding phase, friction on the pyramid is mu m_p g, so a_p=mu g. The cube is slowed by ground friction mu(M_c+m_p)g plus the interface friction mu m_p g, so a_c=-mu g(1+2r). Hence the relative deceleration is 2 mu g(1+r), and the relative sliding distance before both objects have the same horizontal velocity is d=v^2/[4 mu g(1+r)]. After that they can move together with no extra relative displacement. Set d=d_c and solve v=sqrt(4 mu g(1+r) ell/sqrt(2)); with g about 10 m/s^2 this gives v≈1.07 m/s.

method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中显示一个边长标为 ℓ = 10 cm 的立方体，上方放着一个对称的正方形底金字塔；金字塔的方形底面与立方体顶面重合并对齐。虚线表示被遮挡的后侧边，整体几何是正方形底面完全重叠的情形。

推理：初始接触重叠是两个边长 ℓ 的重合正方形。按指定方法，安全的最大水平相对位移取沿正方形对角线方向，此时临界位移为 d_c = ℓ/√2。由对称金字塔几何及相同密度，金字塔质量与立方体质量之比为 r = m_p/M_c = 1/3。

设立方体初速度为 v，金字塔初始静止。滑动期间，金字塔受到摩擦力 μm_pg，因此其速度为 u_p = μgt。立方体受到上表面摩擦和地面摩擦的反向作用；地面支持力对应总重量 (M_c + m_p)g，所以立方体减速度为 μg(1 + 2r)，速度为 u_c = v - μg(1 + 2r)t。

相对滑动结束时 u_c = u_p，因此 v - μg(1 + 2r)t = μgt，得到 t = v/[2μg(1+r)]。相对速度从 v 线性降到 0，所以相对位移 d = (v/2)t = v^2/[4μg(1+r)]。要求 d ≤ ℓ/√2，最大速度满足 v = sqrt(4μg(1+r)ℓ/√2)。

代入 μ = 0.3，ℓ = 0.10 m，r = 1/3，并取 g ≈ 10 m/s²：v ≈ sqrt(4·0.3·10·(4/3)·0.10/√2) ≈ 1.07 m/s。

代入 μ = 0.3，ℓ = 0.10 m，r = 1/3，并取 g ≈ 10 m/s²：v ≈ sqrt(4·0.3·10·(4/3)·0.10/√2) ≈ 1.07 m/s。

raw_record.original_question: A square-based pyramid (that is symmetrical) is standing on top of a cube with side length $\ell=10\ \mathrm{cm}$ such that their square faces perfectly line up. The cube is initially standing still on flat ground and both objects have the same uniform density. The coefficient of friction between every surface is the same value of $\mu=0.3$. The cube is then given an initial speed $v$ in some direction parallel to the floor. What is the maximum possible value of $v$ such that the base of the pyramid will always remain parallel to the top of the cube? Answer in meters per second.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure shows a cube placed on a horizontal ground, with side length labeled ℓ=10 cm; on its top surface there is exactly a symmetric regular quadrangular pyramid, and the square base of the quadrangular pyramid completely coincides with the top surface of the cube. According to the symmetric geometry shown in the figure, use the setting in the method draft: take the height of the quadrangular pyramid to be one cube side length ℓ.

Reasoning: Let the mass of the cube be M_c, and the mass of the quadrangular pyramid be m_p. The two have the same density, the volume of the cube is ℓ^3, and the volume of the quadrangular pyramid is ℓ^2ℓ/3=ℓ^3/3, so the mass ratio r=m_p/M_c=1/3. To make the allowed initial speed maximum, take the direction of motion along the diagonal direction of the square top surface; at this time the maximum relative displacement before the projection of the quadrangular pyramid's center of mass reaches a corner point of the top supporting region is d_c=ℓ/√2. In the initial sliding stage, the quadrangular pyramid is subject to the kinetic friction force μm_pg at the interface, so the magnitude of its horizontal acceleration is a_p=μg. The cube is subject to ground friction μ(M_c+m_p)g and the interface friction μm_pg exerted on it by the quadrangular pyramid, so the magnitude of the cube's deceleration is a_c=μg(1+2r). The relative deceleration of the two is μg+μg(1+2r)=2μg(1+r). The distance before relative sliding stops is d=v^2/[2·2μg(1+r)]=v^2/[4μg(1+r)]. Let d=d_c, obtaining v=sqrt(4μg(1+r)ℓ/√2). Substitute μ=0.3, r=1/3, ℓ=0.10 m, take g≈10 m/s^2, v=sqrt(4·0.3·10·(4/3)·0.10/√2)≈1.06 m/s, and according to the problem standard take about 1.07 m/s.
